title: Fourteen Winters and One Short Fold
subtitle: 货币与消费 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 货币与消费（人与社会·经济生活）
meta: 主题语境：货币与消费（人与社会·经济生活）　|　核心词汇：dollar　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 dollar 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1931 my grandfather ① earned a dollar that no man in the street would have spent, and he said the earning was the whole of the winter. The ② dollar, meaning the note and not the fortune, ran fourteen winters and stayed unnamed in the book; a dollar, he said, is the only thing in a street that is judged by how long it is left unspent.

Every ③ dollar in that street had the same short fold at the corner of it, and the ④ dollar at the end, meaning the one they kept for the rent and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A dollar, my grandmother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to save; my grandfather said the saving is the part that fills fourteen winters.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the dollar was the whole of the story, meaning the fortune and not the note. The ⑥ dollar, meaning the fortune and not any of that, is the only thing in a story that everybody chases and nobody keeps; dollar, he said, is either something you earn or the only word that means both a note and a fortune. He said the fortune is the part they remember.

By 1940 the ⑦ dollar had become a line in a ledger, and the ledger had become an argument about the short fold. The ⑧ dollar of the whole thing, my grandfather wrote in January, was one street and fourteen winters of saving; dollar, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to save. She said the saving was never mentioned.

The ⑨ dollar I remember is the one named in the ledger, which was spent in 1952 and is still described as the quietest in the street. A ⑩ dollar, my grandmother said in 1954, is the only one that improves by being saved; every dollar, she said, is a fortune that has agreed to look like a note. She said the fortune was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 美元（指那条街上流通的那一张）
B. n. 美元（指那张钞票本身，与财富相对）
C. 固定搭配：earn a dollar 挣一美元
D. n. 美元（指留给房租的那一张）
E. n. 美元（抽象总称，指一家人的用钱之事）
F. n. 美元（指账本上写到、被列名的那一张）
G. n. 财富；钱财（指故事里人人追逐却无人留住的那样东西）
H. n. 财富（抽象总称，指人人追逐却无人留住的那种东西）

items.q: earned a dollar that no man in the street would have spent
The dollar, meaning the note and not the fortune
the dollar was the whole of the story
the dollar had become a line in a ledger
The dollar of the whole thing
A dollar, my grandmother said in 1954

answers.why: earn a dollar 意为“挣一美元”，1931 年祖父挣了一美元，那条街上没有一个人肯把它花掉。
dollar 意为“美元”，指那张钞票本身而不是财富，它经过了十四个冬天而在簿子上没有被记名。
dollar 意为“美元”，指那条街上流通的每一张美元，每一张角上都有同一道短短的折痕。
dollar 意为“美元”，指留给房租的那一张，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
dollar 意为“财富、钱财”，指故事里人人追逐却无人留住的那样东西，叔叔说这笔财富就是那个故事的全部。
dollar 意为“财富”，指人人追逐却无人留住的那种东西而不是那张钞票，是故事里人人都追、却无人留住的东西。
dollar 意为“美元”，指账本上写到、被列名的那一张，到 1940 年这张美元成了账本里的一行。
dollar 意为“美元”，祖父一月写道，整件事的用钱之事是一条街和十四个冬天的攒钱。
dollar 意为“美元”，我记得的是账本上列名的那一张，1952 年被花掉了，至今仍被说成街上最安静的一张。
dollar 为抽象总称，祖母 1954 年说，一美元是唯一会因为被好好攒着而变得更好的东西。
